Step 1: run_m

YuKi

Source: vignettes/demo/CODE/test_1_run_m.Rmd
test_1_run_m.Rmd
library(binaryRL)
## Package 'binaryRL' Version:  0.8.10
head(binaryRL::Mason_2024_Exp2)
##   Subject Block Trial Frame L_choice R_choice L_reward R_reward Sub_Choose
## 1       1     1     1  Gain        A        B       36       40          B
## 2       1     1     2  Gain        A        B       36       40          B
## 3       1     1     3  Loss        C        D      -36      -40          D
## 4       1     1     4  Loss        D        C      -40      -36          D
## 5       1     1     5  Loss        D        C      -40      -36          D
## 6       1     1     6  Gain        A        B       36       40          A
##   NetWorth   RT
## 1       40 6855
## 2       80 7089
## 3       40 5147
## 4        0 1531
## 5      -40 1859
## 6       -4 1910

TD 

binaryRL.res <- binaryRL::run_m(
  data = binaryRL::Mason_2024_Exp2,                    
  id = 1,                       
  eta = c(0.123),  
  tau = c(0.789),
  n_params = 2,            
  n_trials = 360,            
  mode = "fit"
)

summary(binaryRL.res)
##   This fitting was performed assuming the agent's initial values for 
##       each option are based on their first encounter, and the agent chooses 
##       randomly when trial count is less than or equal to1.

  data = binaryRL::Mason_2024_Exp2,

  n_params = 3,
  n_trials = 360,
  eta = c(0.123, 0.456),
